tasks.title: Implement PRD to Gherkin Parser Logic
tasks.description: Develop the core parsing logic to extract requirements from PRD content and convert them into structured Gherkin scenarios
tasks.details: Create a parser module that can read PRD content and identify key requirements, user stories, and functional specifications. Map each requirement to a Gherkin feature with appropriate scenarios using Given/When/Then format. Handle edge cases where PRD content cannot be mapped to valid Gherkin syntax. Implement validation to ensure all generated Gherkin follows proper syntax rules.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for parser logic with various PRD formats, validation tests for Gherkin syntax correctness, edge case testing for malformed or ambiguous PRD content

subtasks.title: Implement PRD Content Analysis Module
subtasks.description: Create natural language processing module to analyze PRD text structure and identify requirements patterns

subtasks.title: Build Requirement Extraction Algorithms
subtasks.description: Implement intelligent algorithms to extract structured requirements from unstructured PRD text
subtasks.details: Create extraction algorithms that can parse different PRD formats and extract key requirement components including actors, actions, conditions, and expected outcomes. Implement context-aware parsing that understands requirement hierarchies and relationships. Handle various text formats including markdown, plain text, and structured documents.

subtasks.title: Develop Gherkin Syntax Mapping Engine
subtasks.description: Create mapping system that converts extracted requirements into proper Gherkin Given/When/Then syntax
subtasks.details: Implement intelligent mapping algorithms that translate requirement components into Gherkin syntax elements. Create rules for mapping conditions to Given statements, actions to When statements, and outcomes to Then statements. Ensure proper Gherkin keyword usage and syntax compliance with BDD standards.

subtasks.title: Implement Scenario Generation Logic
subtasks.description: Build the core logic that generates complete Gherkin scenarios from mapped requirement components
subtasks.details: Create scenario generation algorithms that combine mapped Gherkin elements into complete, executable scenarios. Implement feature grouping logic that organizes related scenarios under appropriate Feature headers. Add scenario naming conventions and duplicate detection to ensure clean, organized output.

subtasks.title: Create Edge Case Handling System
subtasks.description: Implement comprehensive handling for ambiguous, incomplete, or unparseable PRD content
subtasks.details: Develop robust error handling for PRD content that cannot be cleanly mapped to Gherkin scenarios. Create fallback mechanisms for incomplete requirements and ambiguous text. Implement content validation that identifies and flags problematic sections while continuing to process valid content.

subtasks.title: Build Gherkin Validation Rules Engine
subtasks.description: Implement validation system to ensure all generated Gherkin follows proper syntax and semantic rules
subtasks.details: Create comprehensive validation rules that check generated Gherkin for syntax correctness, semantic validity, and BDD best practices. Implement validation for proper keyword usage, scenario structure, and step formatting. Add validation for feature file organization and naming conventions.

subtasks.title: Develop Parser Testing Framework
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive testing framework for validating parser functionality with various PRD formats and edge cases
subtasks.details: Build automated testing framework that validates parser performance across different PRD formats, content types, and edge cases. Create test suites for requirement extraction accuracy, Gherkin syntax correctness, and error handling robustness. Implement regression testing for parser improvements and bug fixes.

tasks.title: Create Feature File Generation Engine
tasks.description: Build the engine that generates .feature files from parsed PRD requirements using valid Gherkin syntax
tasks.details: Implement the core engine that takes parsed PRD requirements and generates properly formatted .feature files. Ensure all files use valid Gherkin syntax with Feature, Scenario, Given/When/Then structure. Include proper file naming conventions that sanitize titles for filesystem compatibility. Add error handling for invalid scenarios and graceful failure modes.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration tests for complete PRD-to-feature file generation, Gherkin syntax validation tests, file naming sanitization tests, error handling verification

subtasks.title: Create Gherkin Feature File Template System
subtasks.description: Design and implement the base template structure for generating .feature files with proper Gherkin syntax
subtasks.details: Create template classes and structures that define the standard Gherkin format including Feature headers, Scenario blocks, and Given/When/Then step formatting. Include configurable template variables for feature names, descriptions, and scenarios. Ensure templates follow Cucumber best practices and syntax requirements.

subtasks.title: Implement Gherkin Syntax Formatting Engine
subtasks.description: Build the core formatter that converts parsed PRD requirements into valid Gherkin syntax
subtasks.details: Implement syntax validation and formatting logic that ensures all generated content follows proper Gherkin structure. Include keyword formatting (Feature, Scenario, Given, When, Then, And, But), proper indentation, line breaks, and comment handling. Add syntax validation to prevent invalid Gherkin output.

subtasks.title: Create File Naming and Sanitization System
subtasks.description: Implement robust file naming conventions and sanitization for cross-platform compatibility
subtasks.details: Create file naming logic that converts feature titles into valid filesystem names. Implement sanitization for special characters, length limits, and reserved words. Ensure cross-platform compatibility (Windows, macOS, Linux) and handle naming conflicts with incremental numbering or timestamps.

subtasks.title: Implement Comprehensive Error Handling
subtasks.description: Build error handling system for file generation failures and invalid input scenarios
subtasks.details: Implement error handling for file system operations, template processing failures, invalid Gherkin syntax, and sanitization issues. Create informative error messages and graceful failure modes. Include logging for debugging and recovery mechanisms for partial failures.

subtasks.title: Create Output Validation System
subtasks.description: Implement validation system to verify generated .feature files meet Gherkin standards
subtasks.details: Build validation logic that checks generated .feature files for proper Gherkin syntax, completeness, and structural integrity. Include automated testing of generated files against Gherkin parsers. Validate feature structure, scenario completeness, and step syntax correctness.

tasks.title: Implement TTS Flag for Taskmaster Commands

- Integrate with system TTS engines (Windows SAPI, macOS say command, Linux espeak/festival)
- Create TTS configuration options in the configuration management system
- Add voice selection options (male/female, different languages if available)
- Implement audio output settings (volume, speed, pitch)

- Add option to read entire task lists or individual task details
- Implement TTS for command confirmations and error messages
- Create TTS output formatting to make spoken text more natural (removing markdown, formatting numbers/dates appropriately)
- Add configuration option to enable/disable TTS globally

**Duplicate Save Prevention Testing for TTS Implementation:**

Since TTS functionality involves configuration persistence and potential concurrent operations, implement specific tests to prevent duplicate saves in the TTS context:

- Test TTS configuration saves to prevent duplicate entries in configuration files when users rapidly change voice settings, volume, or other audio parameters
- Validate that TTS engine initialization doesn't create duplicate configuration entries when switching between different TTS engines (Windows SAPI, macOS say, Linux espeak)
- Test concurrent TTS operations to ensure audio output settings aren't duplicated when multiple commands with --tts flag run simultaneously
- Verify that TTS preference saves are atomic and don't result in corrupted or duplicate configuration data during rapid user interactions
- Implement unique constraint checks for TTS configuration entries to prevent duplicate voice profiles or audio settings
- Test TTS configuration persistence across application restarts to ensure settings aren't duplicated on reload
- Validate that TTS error logging doesn't create duplicate log entries when TTS engines fail or fallback mechanisms activate
- Test edge cases where users rapidly toggle global TTS enable/disable settings to prevent duplicate configuration states
- Ensure TTS-related task metadata (like audio output preferences per task) doesn't create duplicate entries in tasks.json
- Implement locking mechanisms for TTS configuration file operations to prevent race conditions during concurrent access

This testing should be integrated with the existing TTS test strategy to ensure robust duplicate prevention across all TTS-related save operations.
